messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate observed for CatalystCorp private VPC egress via dedicated-pool-12 in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
oncall-ingrid: Saw it, paging network-sre and dedicated owner. I'm on the line. CatalinaCorp reported spike ~10:12 UTC.
network-sre-max: joining. Can someone paste the initial metric/graph? I see increased packet drops and failed health checks to NLB target group.
platform-eng-hoa: grabbing logs from dedicated-pool-12. Early signs: conntrack counters near limit and lots of SYN retries to external endpoints. NLB target health shows intermittent 503/502.
se-customer-success-anna: Catalyst oncall (catalyst-oncall) says customer traffic is degraded for API v1 and webhooks are dropping. They can share recent curl traces.
catalyst-oncall: confirming — clients see connection resets and 502s. TTL on our customer DNS is 60s. Noticed traffic bouncing between two NLB IPs.
dedicated-owner-raj: quick inventory: dedicated-pool-12 sits in customer's VPC via Private Deployment. Egress flows go through nat-gw-03 and an inline egress NLB used for health checks. Security groups haven't changed in past 24h per audit.
network-sre-max: can we confirm conntrack exhaustion? paste /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count and nf_conntrack_max.
platform-eng-hoa: running now on box pool-proxy-7:

```
$ cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
1048574
$ cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
1048576
```

platform-eng-hoa: that's 99.999% full.
security-ops-tom: that explains the SYN/RESET behavior. Conntrack hits drop new flows causing TCP failures.
oncall-ingrid: impact: all CatalystCorp endpoints behind that egress path will see failures until freed or we route traffic elsewhere. Need mitigation plan now.
network-sre-max: mitigation options:
  1) Increase nf_conntrack_max (quick, but risk memory pressure) — temporary.
  2) Drain problematic clients via iptables to reduce sessions.
  3) Reroute egress to fallback NAT/egress-proxy we control.
  4) Force short DNS failover by updating DNS to fallback NLB (but DNS TTL 60s so quick).

Which to do first?
platform-eng-hoa: I'll create a temporary egress-proxy container in dedicated-pool-12 to terminate/aggregate connections and reduce conntrack load. Also bump conntrack_max as a stopgap.
dedicated-owner-raj: concur. I'll own the deployment and coord with infra-bastion. @deploy-bot please run canary.
deploy-bot: triggered: deploy egress-proxy-canary on pool-proxy-8 (image: rwd/egress-aggregator:v2.1.3). Rolling canary now.
network-sre-max: before we flip anything, let's drop large idle sessions: applying conntrack cleanup for SYN_RECV/ESTABLISHED > 300s to reclaim slots.

```
# clear old conntracks (careful)
conntrack -L | awk '$6 > 300 {print $0}' | wc -l
conntrack -D --orig-port-src 0
```

platform-eng-hoa: increased nf_conntrack_max from 1048576 -> 1572864 on pool-proxy-7 (sysctl applied). Monitoring memory.
platform-eng-hoa: canary egress-proxy is up. Proxy is healthy and showing aggregated connections ~120k. Initial latency looks fine.
network-sre-max: good. Start shifting a small percentage of customer egress to proxy by updating route table for one AZ.
platform-eng-hoa: updating route table rtb-cc-az1: redirect 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop -> proxy-eni-09 for Catalyst subnet.

```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-cc-az1 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-09
```

platform-eng-hoa: route applied in AZ1. Monitoring now.
oncall-ingrid: customer impact should drop for AZ1 only. @catalyst-oncall can you hit endpoints and report?
catalyst-oncall: AZ1 tests look much better — success rate ~99.8%. AZ2 still errors.
network-sre-max: start rolling AZ2 once we verify conntrack relief. Also, lower conntrack timeout for unestablished flows to 60s as temporary.
security-ops-tom: note: lowering timeouts could affect long-lived webhook connections. Customer confirmed acceptable for now.
platform-eng-hoa: applied sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=432000 -> 300 (reduced for idle). Will revert later.

```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```

deploy-bot: canary metrics: error rate dropped from 12% -> 1.1% for egress traffic routed via proxy.
se-customer-success-anna: passing this update to Catalyst. They ack mitigation and asked for ETA to full fix.
network-sre-max: parallel action: NLB health checks were mis-targeting a previous proxy IP that had been removed yesterday — health check flapping contributed to failover churn. @dns-eng-li can you confirm DNS A records for catalyst-egress.example.com?
dns-eng-li: checking. Catalyst DNS CNAME points to internal-nlb-legacy.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com which maps to IPs that include the removed ENI. TTL is 60s.

```
$ dig +short catalyst-egress.example.com
10.12.45.9
10.12.45.10
```

dns-eng-li: recommend updating CNAME to currently-active nlb-proxy-usw2 and then lower TTL to 30 for quick propagation.
platform-eng-hoa: we prefer to avoid wholesale DNS swap until we confirm proxy stability. Instead, we'll update route tables and increase NLB target group deregistration timeout so targets don't oscillate.
network-sre-max: set target group deregistration delay to 300s and connection draining to smooth the health transitions.

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=slow_start.duration_seconds,Value=30 Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=300
```

platform-eng-hoa: applied. Health check failures decreased. Conntrack pressure dropping — count now ~350k.
platform-eng-hoa: initiating AZ2 route shift to proxy-eni-11.

```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-cc-az2 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-11
```

network-sre-max: both AZs now routing through egress-proxy. Observed 5xxs fall to <0.5% overall. CPU on proxy nodes stable.
oncall-ingrid: good. Start cleanup actions: revert aggressive sysctl after 1 hour of stability and schedule footprint increase for nf_conntrack_max on pool nodes as long-term.
security-ops-tom: will open a security PR to ensure conntrack tuning is documented and approved for private deploys. Also verifying no SG overly permissive rules introduced during mitigation.
dedicated-owner-raj: post-incident plan: replace nat-gw-03 with managed egress cluster that pre-aggregates connections, and add conntrack autoscaling playbook. I'll schedule windows with Catalyst for a maintenance change.
se-customer-success-anna: Catalyst requests timeline for a full root-cause and a postmortem. ETA for draft?
oncall-ingrid: we'll have a preliminary incident report in 3 hours and a full postmortem in 48 hours. Tagging @security-ops-tom and @dedicated-owner-raj as owners.
catalyst-oncall: thanks — they want a short note for their compliance team. Please include DNS, conntrack saturation, and mitigation steps.
dns-eng-li: also recommend they rotate any hard-coded ENI references — their infra had a static mapping to legacy NLB IPs.
platform-eng-hoa: adding commands and exact sysctl changes to the incident doc. Also backing up proxy logs: /var/log/egress-proxy/catalyst/YYYYMMDD.log

```
# example snippet showing aggregated connect counts
2024-06-11T10:15:42Z - proxy stats: active_conns=120345, new_conns_per_s=420, avg_conn_duration=12s
```

deploy-bot: rolling back canary not needed. Will convert canary -> stable once postmortem complete.
oncall-ingrid: final steps: keep egress-proxy in place, monitor for 2 hours, revert sysctl relaxations after 1h, prepare RFC for permanent nat/egress redesign. I'll update status page and send customer note.
se-customer-success-anna: sending templated message to Catalyst: mitigation summary + next steps.
security-ops-tom: I've started a Jira INC-2319 for follow-up (conntrack autoscale + docs). Assigning to raj and max.
network-sre-max: monitoring dashboards look stable. I'll stand by for 2h then start reverting quick fixes in coordination.
platform-eng-hoa: note: we also found an unrelated backup job that opened many outbound connections to third-party analytics — huge fanout contributed to the spike. We'll include that in RCA.
oncall-ingrid: thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated for now. Will keep thread open for postmortem inputs. :thumbsup:
